svg.text: A microphone turns pressure into a voltage. An analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) measures that voltage at fixed moments – 48 000 times a second in
an earbud – and rounds each measurement to the nearest of 2ⁿ levels. Real audio uses 16 or 24 bits; three are drawn here. To capture a tone you must
sample more than twice as fast as it vibrates (Nyquist), which is why 48 kHz comfortably covers the 20 kHz limit of hearing. The speaker runs it
backwards: a DAC turns numbers into voltages, the voice coil into motion, the diaphragm into pressure.
Earshot field manual · 02 · signals to bits
